title_en: Phones away all day? Smartphones in secondary schools
title_he: בלי טלפון כל היום? סמארטפונים בבית הספר התיכון
prompt: Argue whether secondary schools should require students to lock away their smartphones for the whole school day, including breaks, and respond to opposing views.

instructions.en: Write an argumentative essay of 450-550 words for a general reader, such as the readers of a school or local news website. State your position clearly in the introduction (your thesis). Develop at least three supporting arguments, each in its own paragraph, with a reason, evidence or a specific example, and an explanation of how it supports your thesis. Evidence can be specific examples, reasoned explanation or your own experience described precisely; do not invent statistics or present guesses as facts. At this stage, focus on the opposing view: choose the strongest objection to your position (not the easiest one to answer), state it fairly, attribute it (for example, "Some parents argue that..."), and signal it clearly so that the reader does not mistake it for your own view. Then answer it with reasons. End with a conclusion that restates your thesis in new words and adds no new arguments.
instructions.he: כתבו חיבור טיעוני באורך 450–550 מילים. הציגו במבוא עמדה ברורה (תזה), ופתחו לפחות שלושה טיעונים תומכים, כל אחד בפסקה נפרדת, עם ראיה או דוגמה ספציפית והסבר של הקשר לתזה. בשלב הזה הדגש הוא על העמדה הנגדית: בחרו את ההתנגדות החזקה ביותר (לא את הקלה ביותר לתשובה), הציגו אותה בהגינות, ציינו מי טוען אותה, סמנו בבירור שזו לא העמדה שלכם, וענו עליה בנימוקים. סיימו בסיכום שמנסח את התזה מחדש במילים אחרות ואינו מוסיף טיעונים חדשים. אל תמציאו נתונים או סטטיסטיקות.

required_elements: a clear thesis in the introduction
at least three supporting arguments, each in its own paragraph
relevant evidence or a specific example for each argument, with the link to the thesis explained
the strongest opposing view, stated fairly, attributed and clearly signalled
a rebuttal that answers the opposing view with reasons
a conclusion that restates the thesis without adding new arguments

checklist.en: Claim: my thesis takes a clear, debatable position on locking phones away all day, and it appears in the introduction.
checklist.he: טענה: התזה שלי מציגה עמדה ברורה שאפשר להתווכח עליה, והיא מופיעה כבר במבוא.

checklist.en: Reasons: I give at least three different reasons, one per paragraph, and each one supports my thesis, not a different point.
checklist.he: נימוקים: יש לי לפחות שלושה נימוקים שונים, כל אחד בפסקה משלו, וכולם תומכים בתזה שלי ולא בנקודה אחרת.

checklist.en: Evidence: each reason has specific evidence or an example, and I explain how it supports the reason. I have not invented any numbers.
checklist.he: ראיות: לכל נימוק יש ראיה או דוגמה ספציפית, והסברתי איך היא תומכת בו. לא המצאתי מספרים.

checklist.en: Counterargument: I state the strongest opposing view fairly, in words the other side would accept, and signal it clearly ("Critics argue that...").
checklist.he: טיעון נגדי: הצגתי את העמדה הנגדית החזקה ביותר בהגינות, כך שגם הצד השני היה מקבל את הניסוח, ציינתי מי טוען אותה וסימנתי בבירור שזו לא העמדה שלי ("Critics argue that...").

checklist.en: Rebuttal: I answer the objection with reasons or evidence, not with dismissal, and if I accept part of it, my thesis says so.
checklist.he: הפרכה: עניתי לטיעון הנגדי בנימוקים או בראיות ולא רק דחיתי אותו, ואם קיבלתי חלק ממנו, התזה שלי משקפת את זה.

checklist.en: Conclusion: my conclusion restates my thesis in new words and adds no new arguments.
checklist.he: סיכום: הסיכום מנסח מחדש את התזה במילים אחרות ואינו מוסיף טיעונים חדשים.

scaffold.en: Decide your position and write it as one sentence: "Secondary schools should / should not require ... because ...".
scaffold.he: החליטו מה עמדתכם ונסחו אותה במשפט אחד: "Secondary schools should / should not require ... because ...".

scaffold.en: List four or five reasons for your position, then keep the three strongest. Next to each, note one specific example or piece of evidence.
scaffold.he: רשמו ארבעה או חמישה נימוקים לעמדתכם ובחרו את שלושת החזקים ביותר. ליד כל נימוק רשמו דוגמה או ראיה ספציפית.

scaffold.en: Imagine a reader who disagrees, such as a parent or a student who uses the phone for schoolwork. Write down their best objection, not the weakest one, and ask: would they accept my description of their view?
scaffold.he: דמיינו קורא שלא מסכים איתכם, למשל הורה או תלמיד שמשתמש בטלפון ללימודים. רשמו את ההתנגדות הטובה ביותר שלו, לא את החלשה ביותר, ושאלו את עצמכם: האם הוא היה מסכים לאופן שבו תיארתי את עמדתו?

scaffold.en: Plan six paragraphs: introduction with thesis, argument 1, argument 2, argument 3, opposing view and your response, conclusion.
scaffold.he: תכננו שש פסקאות: מבוא עם תזה, טיעון 1, טיעון 2, טיעון 3, עמדה נגדית והתשובה שלכם, סיכום.

scaffold.en: Phrases for presenting the opposing view: Some parents argue that... / Critics of a full-day ban point out that... / It is often claimed that... / Admittedly, ...
scaffold.he: ביטויים להצגת העמדה הנגדית: Some parents argue that... / Critics of a full-day ban point out that... / It is often claimed that... / Admittedly, ...

scaffold.en: Phrases for responding: However, this overlooks... / While this is true in some cases, ... / This concern is valid, but it could be addressed by...
scaffold.he: ביטויים לתשובה: However, this overlooks... / While this is true in some cases, ... / This concern is valid, but it could be addressed by...

exemplar.outline:
Parallel prompt (not your question; read this only after you have written your own essay): Argue whether secondary schools should start the school day one hour later, and respond to opposing views.

Thesis: Secondary schools should start one hour later, because students who are less tired are likely to learn more, mornings become safer and calmer, and the practical problems can be solved.

1. Introduction: the familiar picture of a half-asleep first lesson; the proposal in one sentence; thesis.
2. Argument 1, learning: many teenagers find it hard to fall asleep early, so an early start cuts their sleep. Example: the same student taking a test in the first lesson and in a late-morning lesson.
3. Argument 2, safety and health: rushed, sleepy journeys in the dark in winter; breakfast skipped.
4. Argument 3, punctuality: fewer late arrivals, so lessons start on time and teachers spend less time dealing with lateness.
5. Opposing view and response (annotated below): parents who leave for work early need their children to leave early too. Concede that the problem is real; answer with supervised early opening of the library and sports hall.
6. Conclusion: restate the thesis in new words; suggest a one-year trial in a few schools.
exemplar.annotated_paragraph:
From the exemplar essay on the parallel prompt above (paragraph 5: opposing view and response)

[1] Many parents, however, raise a serious objection: if school starts later, children whose parents leave for work at 7:30 would either be alone at home or arrive at a closed school. [2] This concern is reasonable, especially for families with younger children and no flexible working hours. [3] Yet it is a problem of supervision, not of learning, and it can be solved without making every student start the day tired. [4] Schools could open the library and sports hall from 7:45 with one member of staff on duty, so that students who need to arrive early have a safe place to read, finish homework or exercise. [5] The cost of this supervision is small compared with the benefit of a full day of lessons taught to students who are awake enough to learn.

Notes
[1] Signals the opposing view ("however") and attributes it to a group (parents), so the reader knows it is not the writer's own view.
[2] Concedes what is true in the objection. Fairness makes the response more convincing, not weaker.
[3] Rebuttal move: reframes the problem (supervision, not learning) instead of dismissing it.
[4] A specific, practical answer: it shows that the objection can be met, not just denied.
[5] Weighs the two sides and links back to the thesis (learning).
